sources.title: MAA/RN/2025/04 — Use of Artificial Intelligence within Systems and Equipment subject to MRP design assurance processes
sources.publisher: UK Ministry of Defence, Military Aviation Authority
sources.jurisdiction: UK military aviation; systems and equipment subject to MAA Regulatory Publications design-assurance processes
sources.inspection_scope: Downloaded and inspected all five pages of Version 5.0. The inspection covers scope, effective status, certified-air-system process, frozen-model/ODD recommendation, architectural mitigation, non-compliances and summary. This is an authority notice, but it describes itself as informative guidance and requires applicant-specific MAA agreement.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 1–2, paragraphs 2–4, Scope, Implementation and Background
regions.excerpt: This guidance is effective immediately and represents the MAA’s current position with respect to AI technologies.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 2–3, paragraphs 5–8, Certified Air Systems
regions.excerpt: For Certified Air Systems, the Applicant should raise a Military Certification Review Item (MCRI) for MAA agreement.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, paragraphs 13–14, Non-Compliances and Summary
regions.excerpt: It is not currently possible to be prescriptive on resolving these issues without architectural mitigation.

sources.limitations: A current MAA position for the UK Defence Air Environment is neither a civil-airworthiness approval nor a published product safety case. The notice is guidance/informative correspondence; MCRI/ATM-ARI agreement and the underlying evidence remain applicant-specific and non-public here.

sources.title: NPA 2025-07 (B) — Proposed detailed specifications and associated acceptable means of compliance and guidance material for AI trustworthiness (DS.AI)
sources.jurisdiction: European aviation domains within the EU AI Act aviation framework; proposed DS.AI material
sources.inspection_scope: Downloaded and inspected the full 43-page Notice of Proposed Amendment. Inspected the title/status, scope, operational-domain and risk material, system-development assurance, supervised-ML learning assurance, continuous risk assessment and monitoring provisions.

regions.excerpt: The following cases are excluded from the scope of DS.AI: (1) AI-based systems presenting a risk directly contributing to the potential for fatalities or multiple life-threatening injuries

regions.locator: PDF pp. 24–26, DS.AI.150 and AMC1/AMC2 AI.150
regions.excerpt: A system development assurance process should be planned and implemented

regions.locator: PDF pp. 31–33, DS.AI.160 and AMC1 AI.160(a)
regions.excerpt: The AI-based system should be designed with means for in-service monitoring and recording to support the continuous risk assessment

sources.limitations: The document is explicitly a Notice of Proposed Amendment and labels its material ‘Proposed DS.AI’; it is not a final EASA decision. Its scope is Level 1/2 high-risk AI and expressly excludes systems directly contributing to fatalities/multiple life-threatening injuries, as well as certain online-learning and logic/knowledge-based systems. The proposed recognition of ED-324/ARP6983 must be checked against the standard's publication status.

sources.title: WG-114 — Artificial Intelligence
sources.inspection_scope: Downloaded and inspected the current WG-114 page and its deliverables table. The page identifies ED-324 as Draft and provides a target publication date. It is a work-program status page, not the draft standard itself or an authority recognition decision.

regions.excerpt: ED-324 | Development and Assurance considerations for Aeronautical Systems and Equipment implemented with Machine Learning | Draft | Target Publication Date: 31/12/2026

sources.limitations: A standards-body page establishes only the displayed status at inspection time. It does not disclose ED-324's technical content, prove final publication or establish use as an accepted means of compliance. Check the publisher and relevant authority again before release.

sources.title: Guidance on the Assurance of Machine Learning in Autonomous Systems (AMLAS), Version 1.1
sources.publisher: University of York, Assuring Autonomy International Programme
sources.jurisdiction: Cross-domain research guidance; not an authority approval
sources.inspection_scope: Downloaded and inspected the 54-page Version 1.1 guidance, including introduction, six-stage process, scoping inputs/outputs, safety-requirements allocation, stated scope and offline-supervised-learning focus. Follow-up inspection covered the data requirements, model-learning overfitting and leakage examples, and independent verification guidance on PDF pp. 21–26, 33–35, and 40–41.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 2–3, Introduction and Overview of AMLAS
regions.excerpt: AMLAS scope covers the following ML lifecycle stages: ML safety assurance scoping, safety requirements elicitation, data management, model learning, model verification and model deployment.
The scope of AMLAS is limited to the ML component. As such, this document should not be used in isolation from other standards and guidelines
AMLAS has a primary focus on off-line supervised learning.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 21–23 (printed pp. 20–22), Data Requirements and Examples 8–12
regions.excerpt: ML data requirements shall include consideration of the relevance, completeness, accuracy and balance of the data.

regions.locator: PDF p. 26 (printed p. 25), verification-data challenge and Note 21
regions.excerpt: Verification data is gathered with the aim of testing the models to breaking point.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 33–35 (printed pp. 32–34), Model Learning, Notes 29–30, Activities 10–11 and Note 5
regions.excerpt: A common problem that is encountered when creating a model is overfitting to training data.

regions.locator: PDF pp. 40–41 (printed pp. 39–40), Activity 13 and Notes 31–33
regions.excerpt: All verification activities shall be sufficiently independent from the development activities.

sources.limitations: AMLAS is public research guidance, not a regulator-issued means of compliance or product authorization. It explicitly limits itself to the ML component and expects system/domain assurance inputs; it does not settle a safety threshold, regulator acceptance or a complete aircraft/vehicle approval case.
